title: Neuroscience and architecture: modulating behavior through sensorimotor responses to the built environment
authors: Djebbara, Zakaria; Jensen, Ole B.; Parada, Francisco J.; Gramann, Klaus
review_question: To provide a psychobiological framework describing how environmental features lead to automated sensorimotor responses through neuro-physiological mechanisms underlying attention, and to bridge sensorimotor responses with predictive neurophysiological processes of attention to expose how designed environmental features affect the neural substrate of meaningful experiences.

findings.quote: EFs modulate behavior by biasing the execution of SMRs that are associated with distinct behaviors

findings.consequent: Sensorimotor responses (SMRs) and optic flow processing
findings.quote: this EF-SMR relation is based on early thalamocortical activity that influences how optic flow in primary visual areas of the brain is processed relative to bodily action.

findings.consequent: Predictions (generation and propagation across cortical layers)
findings.quote: the perceptual system is actively engaged in generating predictions that propagate at different cortical layers.

findings.consequent: Correction (level of, relative to sensory signal certainty)
findings.quote: prediction errors are precision-weighted so that the level of correction is relative to the certainty of the sensory signal
optimizing the precision of the signals in the visual system will lead to a stronger bias on the posterior outcome, which also affects the predictions when updated with the posterior distribution.
the thalamus is vital for both synchronizing cortical activity across brain regions, as well as regulating cortical excitability
the pulvinar, being the HO nuclei in the visual system, is actively contributing to the cortico-cortical pathways by way of transthalamic connections

findings.consequent: Information transmission between cortical areas (regulated) and cortical alpha activity (synchronized)
findings.quote: the pulvinar synchronized the activity between cortical areas (visual and temporal cortex), providing evidence that the pulvinar has a critical role in regulating information transmission across the visual cortex.

findings.antecedent: Pulvinar (integration of environmental change and self-motion)
findings.quote: the sensorimotor incongruence can be resolved by attenuating the precision of sensory signals involved with self-motion.

findings.consequent: Affordances (broad network involving covariations, action trajectories, goal-oriented coordination, task/situation)
findings.quote: sensorimotor schemes compose a broad network of affordances that directly involve (i) the agent's sensorimotor covariations, (ii) the reliable action trajectories, (iii) the goal-oriented coordination, and (iv) the task or situation of the agent

affordances reflect the essence of allostasis, which is the anticipatory process that proactively predicts the outcome of a situation before it can have a potentially lethal impact on the homeostatic process

findings.antecedent: Rate of change of sensory information (optic flow)
findings.quote: the notion that the rate of change in sensory impressions, e.g. optical flow in visual sensation, is an important feature for cognition and behavior is conspicuous.

findings.antecedent: Road markings (decreasing distance between white stripes on dangerous curves)
findings.quote: decreasing the distance between the white stripes painted onto the road when approaching the dangerous curves so that the sensory dynamics associated with high velocity is implicitly affecting our attunement causing a change in the scheme network and eventually expressed behaviorally in slowing down.

findings.antecedent: Visual patterns (wide vertical lines on tunnel walls, associated with slower rate of change)
findings.quote: If the vertical lines were wide, which is typically associated with moving with low velocity as it provides a slower rate of change, the participants speeded up significantly as compared to thin vertical lines

findings.consequent: Movement velocity and early perceptual processes (sensorimotor cortex)
findings.quote: the movement-velocity in approaching the door and the early perceptual processes over the sensorimotor cortex reflected the affordances of the door.

findings.antecedent: Floor tile-pattern direction (close to straight line)
findings.quote: participants veered significantly away from the straight trajectory in their baseline when walking over patterns that were close to the straight line, but not if the pattern direction was rotated too far off the straight line.

findings.antecedent: Optical flow (higher frequency of projected lines)
findings.quote: consistently found a decrease in walking speed when the distance between the projected lines decreased, i.e. higher frequency of lines in optical flow.

findings.antecedent: Visual patterns (horizontal lines on tunnel walls)
findings.quote: the horizontal lines made the budgerigars fly significantly faster.

findings.antecedent: Slow cortical alpha rhythm (over occipital areas)
findings.quote: slow cortical alpha rhythm over occipital areas reflect exactly such transmission

synthesis_conclusions: Environmental features implicitly guide behavior by appealing to certain sensory and motor dynamics, leading to automated sensorimotor responses.

The functional link between the designed environment and sensorimotor responses operates through a thalamo-cortical network integrating environmental features with motor aspects of behavior, driven by transthalamic transmission and predictive neuronal dynamics.

Subtle environmental changes, such as road markings, visual patterns, and spatial configurations, can give rise to distinct sensorimotor responses that modulate behavior (e.g., driving speed, walking direction) often without conscious awareness.
Urban structures, whether planned rectangular grids or natural unplanned districts, inherit specific sensorimotor responses that affect cognition and behavior in distinct and automated ways.

Mobile Brain/Body Imaging (MoBi) combined with generative and causal modeling is a promising approach for future studies to investigate cortical areas involved in automatic behavior and quantify the effect of environmental features on neural dynamics.
evidence_gaps: It remains unknown whether the integrative transthalamic pathway accounts for other biases beyond those discussed.
More empirical and modeling studies are needed to better understand how the omnipresent built environment continuously affects the human brain.
limitations: Intracranial studies of transthalamic transmission are remarkably rare in human beings, limiting direct human neurophysiological evidence for some proposed mechanisms.

theory_commitments.specific_claim: Exposure to natural environments can restore directed attention by reducing mental fatigue.
Exposure to natural environments can reduce physiological stress and negative affect.
Cognitive processes are deeply influenced by the body's sensorimotor interactions with the physical environment.
Humans possess an innate tendency to connect with nature and other living systems.

mechanism_chain.description: Environmental features are perceived through sensorimotor systems, leading to neural, physiological, cognitive, and affective changes that ultimately modulate behavior.

steps.from_construct: Exposure to natural elements (e.g., views of greenery)
steps.to_construct: Activation of parasympathetic nervous system / reduced physiological arousal
Improved mood / reduced stress / enhanced cognitive restoration
Modulation of circadian rhythms / melatonin production
Improved sleep quality / alertness / cognitive performance

instruments_used.name: fMRI
instruments_used.description: Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging to measure changes in blood flow related to neural activity.

instruments_used.name: EEG
instruments_used.description: Electroencephalography to measure electrical activity in the brain.

instruments_used.name: EDA
instruments_used.description: Electrodermal Activity (skin conductance) to measure sympathetic nervous system activity.

instruments_used.name: Heart Rate Variability (HRV)
instruments_used.description: Measurement of variations in the time interval between heartbeats.

instruments_used.name: Eye-tracking
instruments_used.description: Technology to measure eye movements and points of gaze.

instruments_used.name: PANAS
instruments_used.description: Positive and Negative Affect Schedule, a self-report questionnaire for mood states.

instruments_used.name: Cognitive performance tasks
instruments_used.description: Various behavioral tasks (e.g., N-back, Stroop, reaction time tasks) to assess cognitive abilities.
